intelArticles.title: FY26 IDT-R Travel Reimbursement Rules and DTS Requirements
intelArticles.summary: The Navy Reserve’s FY26 Inactive Duty Training Travel Reimbursement (IDT-R) policy provides travel reimbursement for eligible Reserve Sailors who live 150 miles or more from their assigned drill location. Eligible participants may receive reimbursement for up to 12 round trips during FY26, subject to available funding. IDT-R travel must be processed through the Defense Travel System (DTS), and participants must have a Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC).
intelArticles.whyItMatters: IDT-R can significantly reduce the out-of-pocket cost of traveling long distances to drill, but reimbursement is not automatic. Sailors must meet billet and assignment eligibility requirements, enroll in the program, follow DTS procedures, and document their expenses. The program is discretionary and may be restricted by funding availability.
intelArticles.details:
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1570, dated January 15, 2026, establishes the FY26 Navy Reserve IDT-R policy and DTS procedures.
Eligibility generally requires the Sailor to be assigned to an eligible “R”-coded billet, be locally assigned with TRUIC and UMUIC aligned, and have a primary drilling location 150 miles or more from the Sailor’s primary residence. Eligible Sailors must apply through the Navy Reserve IDT-R application process.
IDT-R is considered official travel. Participants are required to have a Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC), and use of a Centrally Billed Account (CBA) is not authorized. A DTS authorization and voucher are required for reimbursement.
Eligible participants may receive reimbursement for up to 12 round trips to their drill site during FY26, subject to the applicable reimbursement limits and available IDT-R funding. The Navy identifies IDT-R as discretionary funding, so reimbursement availability may be restricted by budget constraints.
Reimbursable expenses may include qualifying transportation, lodging, meals, rental vehicle expenses, fuel, and tolls when authorized by the policy. Rental vehicles are reimbursable when they are more advantageous to the government than taxi or rideshare transportation; otherwise reimbursement may be limited to the comparable taxi or rideshare cost.
IDT-R cannot duplicate benefits already provided through IDT meals-in-kind or Berthing for Drilling Reservists. The notice establishes specific meal and lodging reimbursement rules for travel days surrounding the IDT period.
Receipts are required for all IDT-R expenses, including meals, rental cars, fuel, and tolls, even where the normal Joint Travel Regulations receipt threshold would not otherwise require one.
When a DTS authorization cannot be approved before travel and an after-the-fact authorization is required, an IDT-R oral-order confirmation letter must be approved by the NRA commanding officer and uploaded with the DTS authorization and voucher. Failure to provide the required letter results in disapproval of the DTS authorization and voucher.
The notice remains in effect for one year or until revised.

intelArticles.title: NAVADMIN 200/26: Annual CBRN Mask Fit Training Required for Reservists
intelArticles.summary: All Active and Reserve Navy personnel must complete annual CBRN protective-mask fit and seal training, with Reserve component implementation plans and readiness tracking required.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: This creates a recurring annual readiness requirement that can affect Reserve training plans and should eventually be represented in Salty Dog's readiness/admin tracking.
intelArticles.details: NAVADMIN 200/26 establishes annual CBRN mask fit and seal training for all Navy personnel, including Reserve personnel. Training includes approved fit testing and a negative-pressure seal check, inspection and preventive maintenance of protective equipment, mask donning, clearing, adjustment and use, plus command-applicable confidence training. For Type I, III and VI duty, ashore and Reserve component commanders were directed to submit implementation plans and strive to have personnel complete the requirement no later than December 31, 2026. Annual completion is documented in FLTMPS.

intelArticles.title: NAVADMIN 106/26 — FY27 Reserve Officer Continuation Moves to Semiannual Boards
intelArticles.summary: Beginning in FY27, eligible Reserve officer retention and continuation cases move from monthly panels to two semiannual boards, with the first FY27 package deadline on November 15, 2026.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: Reserve officers approaching statutory attrition because of age, promotion failures, or years of service now have fewer board opportunities and firm package deadlines to plan around.
intelArticles.details: NAVADMIN 106/26 applies to eligible Selected Reserve, Individual Ready Reserve and Standby Reserve-Active officers; TAR officers are handled separately. Beginning October 1, 2026, the process transitions from monthly panels to semiannual boards. The FY27 boards convene January 18, 2027 and July 19, 2027. For the January board, eligible attrition dates run from February 1 through July 31, 2027 and packages are due by 2359 CST on November 15, 2026. For the July board, eligible attrition dates run from August 1, 2027 through January 31, 2028 and packages are due by 2359 CST on May 15, 2027. Late packages are not accepted.

intelArticles.title: Reserve Component Fairness Act — Prior Active-Duty Retirement Credit Proposal
intelArticles.summary: A new proposal would let qualifying active-duty service performed after January 28, 2008, before joining the Ready Reserve count toward reducing the age for non-regular retired pay.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: This could materially change the retirement-pay start age for some veterans who served on regular active duty before affiliating with the Reserve or National Guard.
intelArticles.details: Rep. Abe Hamadeh announced the Reserve Component Fairness Act on August 24, 2026. Under the proposal, qualifying active-duty service performed after January 28, 2008, could count toward the existing reduced-retirement-age rules even when that service occurred before Ready Reserve affiliation. The proposal would not eliminate the requirement to earn a Reserve retirement: members would still need to satisfy the existing qualifying-service requirements, including 20 qualifying years, and the statutory minimum retirement age would remain 50. As of September 14, 2026, this is a proposal and not enacted law; current Reserve retirement calculations have not changed.

intelArticles.title: Duty Status Reform Act — Four-Category Reserve Duty Framework
intelArticles.summary: House and Senate bills would consolidate the Reserve Component duty-status framework into four categories and align pay and benefits around the new structure.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: If enacted and implemented, the legislation could eventually change how Reserve orders, IDT-like duty, remote assignments, pay, benefits, and Salty Dog terminology are organized.
intelArticles.details: H.R. 6976 and Senate companion S. 4801 have been introduced. The Senate bill creates four categories: Category I active duty, Category II active duty, Category III reserve component duty, and Category IV remote assignments. It would also treat references to inactive duty, inactive-duty training, and inactive duty for training as references to reserve component duty. The introduced Senate text provides a default effective date 10 years after enactment, with a process for an earlier date if DoD, DHS, and VA certify readiness and Congress enacts a law establishing that earlier date. The bills have not become law, so current IDT, AT, ADT, and other duty-status rules remain in effect.

intelArticles.title: FY27 NDAA: House Passes Tiered 5–7% Military Pay Raise
intelArticles.summary: The House-passed FY27 NDAA would provide a tiered basic-pay increase: 7% for E-5 and below, 6% for E-6 through O-3, and 5% for O-4 and above.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: Reserve drill pay is derived from military basic pay, so the final enacted 2027 basic-pay adjustment will flow directly into Reserve drill-pay tables and Salty Dog pay calculations.
intelArticles.details: The House passed H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, on July 22, 2026. The House version supports a 7% increase for E-5 and below, 6% for E-6 through O-3, and 5% for O-4 and above. This is not yet the final 2027 pay table: the Senate must complete its NDAA process, differences must be reconciled, and final legislation must be enacted. Until that occurs, Salty Dog should continue to label FY27 pay figures as proposed rather than effective.

intelArticles.title: Reserve Forces Travel Fairness Act — Rental Car Reimbursement Proposal
intelArticles.summary: H.R. 7593 would authorize reimbursement for rental-vehicle costs tied to qualifying Reserve inactive-duty training or Ready Reserve muster duty performed more than 150 miles from home.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: Non-local Reservists can incur substantial transportation costs around drill periods. If enacted, the proposal could affect travel reimbursement decisions and Salty Dog travel/tax guidance.
intelArticles.details: H.R. 7593, the Reserve Forces Travel Fairness Act, was introduced in the House on February 17, 2026 and referred to the House Armed Services Committee. The bill would amend title 37 to reimburse qualifying rental-motor-vehicle costs for Reserve Component inactive-duty training or Ready Reserve muster duty performed more than 150 miles from a member's permanent residence. The bill is not law, so members should continue using current travel and reimbursement rules unless and until implementing guidance changes.

intelArticles.title: 2027 VA Compensation COLA — August CPI-W Released
intelArticles.summary: August CPI-W is now available, but the 2027 Social Security and VA compensation COLA is not final. The September CPI release is scheduled for October 14.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: Reservists receiving VA disability compensation need the final COLA percentage to estimate 2027 monthly compensation accurately.
intelArticles.details: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported an August 2026 CPI-W index of 328.481, 3.5% above August 2025. The official Social Security COLA is based on the third-quarter CPI-W calculation, so the final percentage cannot be determined until September data are released on October 14, 2026. Congress has also introduced H.R. 8552 and S. 4487, the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026, which would apply the eventual Social Security adjustment to VA disability compensation and DIC effective December 1, 2026. No official 2027 VA compensation rate should be treated as final yet.
intelArticles.sourceName: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — August 2026 CPI

intelArticles.title: Navy Reserve AT Requirement — Current Published Guidance
intelArticles.summary: Current Navy Reserve guidance continues to require satisfactory participation and, for SELRES, normally includes 12–14 days of Annual Training or equivalent qualifying active duty each fiscal year.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: The Drill Calendar and Orders tools should distinguish the standing SELRES participation requirement from proposed future duty-status changes.
intelArticles.details: The Navy Reserve's current RESPERSMAN index lists 1001-010 for satisfactory participation and 1571-010 for Annual Training and Active Duty Training. Published Navy Reserve guidance states that SELRES members normally perform 12–14 days of AT, or equivalent qualifying active duty, within the fiscal year, with waiver procedures available when applicable. This is current guidance, not a newly announced FY27 change. Unit-specific requirements and approved waivers can still affect an individual Sailor's execution plan.

intelArticles.title: Major Richard Star Act — House Discharge Petition Stands at 217
intelArticles.summary: The official House Clerk page lists 217 signatures on Discharge Petition No. 22 for H.R. 2102 — one short of the 218-signature threshold.
intelArticles.whyItMatters: The bill targets the offset affecting certain combat-related Chapter 61 disability retirees with fewer than 20 years of service who cannot currently receive full military retired pay and VA disability compensation concurrently.
intelArticles.details: The Major Richard Star Act is H.R. 2102 in the House and S. 1032 in the Senate. It would expand concurrent receipt for certain combat-related disability retirees retired under Chapter 61 with fewer than 20 years of creditable service. The official House Clerk page for Discharge Petition No. 22 lists 217 signatures, with the latest listed signature dated September 2, 2026. Reaching 218 would advance the discharge process; it would not itself enact the bill. The Major Richard Star Act remains proposed legislation and current payment-offset rules remain in effect unless Congress changes the law.
intelArticles.sourceName: Clerk of the U.S. House — Discharge Petition No. 22
